description: Reviewed target-fit exclusions for the UK terminal battery (schema 2 per #610). Each entry defers one calibration target whose |relative error| breaches the 25% release bound, with the defect diagnosed, tracked, and owned elsewhere; the receipt records the reasoning, approver, adjudication reference, approval date, and expiry. The gate keeps the target BOUND in calibration (exclusion applies to the release fence only, never the solve), reports dormant entries, FAILS stale ones (targets back inside the bound), and FAILS expired ones until the adjudication is renewed, so this register cannot rot.

hmrc.spi_region.income_tax_by_region_125.reason: Calibration competition with the national employment-income bands. At design weights the South East GBP 12,570-15,000 income-tax cell is 11% short of its target (69.6m against 78.3m on the #1063 stack; 62.4m on main) and the national employment-income bands at GBP 12,570-15,000 and 15,000-20,000 are 20% and 31% short (the earners gap the 2026-09-30 build found: too few employees in those bands, half an uprating-within-fixed-bands artefact). The solver fills those bands by raising the weights of low-paid employees everywhere, three-fold on the 200 households that carry most of this cell's gain, and the South East income-tax cell, carried by the same households, overshoots to +32.0% while its total-income sibling lands at +11.2% (main pulls the same cell from -20% to +22.6%). The cell was deferred on 2026-09-18 and retired on microcosm#1012 at +24.5%; deferred four weeks again until the employment-income band support is corrected in the frame or the bands are re-adjudicated, which is where the pull comes from.
